says: A surface said in this observatory: the steps one can take from what is shown - each thing a line is about, once, with how to stand on it. For a shell, for a script, for anyone who walks by saying where to stand.
What is being done now, what is in progress, and what shows and has come to nothing yet: three lenses placed together, asking nothing of their own.

What this observatory shows first: what followed the latest thing the author said; then its own sheet - what is showing and what each waits on - then the perfect form of the whole and how the whole stands to it, then every other lens in view.
Of what a lens shows, only what is held back by the author: what waits on his word.

The pages this observatory publishes: the whole; a page for each place it has in view, each sign, each angle of the perfect form, each decision a sign came to, and each record of work of the last three days with each thing it entered or changed - what the thing says in full, and what is around it - and the pages the places in view offer of their own. Each row is a page: where it is written, what it looks through, and the thing it is the page of.

What is still showing, and what the whole waits on: signs nothing has come of, runs failing on main, what holds work back and by what, what waits only in words, and what would free the most once done - placed together, asking nothing of their own.
What waits on the author: the sheet of what is showing, seen through a lens that keeps only what is held back by him.

What each place has written down as documents - what it is, how to work in it, what it has specified: each file a row, and how it begins. Read where a place is held. All of it is taken in: what is said in a document is said too.
Who takes part: a person or an agent, what they are called, and the other names they go by - so that what waits on someone can be drawn.

Where everything lives: every surface something of this work is kept on - in a place or outside any - what shape it holds there, how it is read now, and what is lacking for it to be read. So that what the ecosystem does not yet consume is in view, beside what it does.
The perfect form of the whole, from each angle it has been described - and beside it what the lenses show of each now: how the whole stands to its own idea, read off and not said.
What the first observatory holds up first, in order, and why: the places a visitor should not miss.
What the Open Commons Observatory shows first: why each star exists and how far it has come, then what is showing and has come to nothing yet, then every other lens in view.
How work is done here: each practice, why it is so, and where it is shown in what was decided - read by any driver, added to as a way of working is settled.

The pages this observatory publishes in the language, beside the engine's: the whole, and a page for each place it has in view - what is around it. Each row is a page: where it is written, what it looks through, and the thing it is the page of.
